name: sheffield-bungalow-land
intent: Bungalow and land sweep (2+ beds, asking ≤ £325k, all-in ≤ £425k; Meersbrook and neighbours, the Endcliffe Park side of S11, and the bungalow suburbs next to them: Norton Lees, Beauchief, Abbey Lane, Ecclesall, Bents Green). BUNGALOWS (incl. dormer and chalet bungalows) AND LAND / BUILDING PLOTS ONLY: no ordinary houses. The buyer wants one big open-plan living-kitchen-dining space with the front door into a hall, and needs only 2 bedrooms. Buy cheap against fundamentals, refurb or build while renting elsewhere, then live in it. Works budget up to about £250k from family loans. For land, judge the house the buyer would build to the finished spec.

vibe.summary: A bungalow or building plot on a quiet owner-occupied street, walkable to a big park, near Meersbrook / Nether Edge / Endcliffe Park. Not an estate of retirement bungalows, not a student area.
likes: big park within 10 min walk (Graves, Meersbrook, Endcliffe, Millhouses, Ecclesall Woods)
wide or deep plot with room to extend or add a dormer
independent high street nearby (Abbeydale Rd, Chesterfield Rd, Sharrow Vale, Ecclesall Rd)
avoid: very steep plots with no access

types: land or building plot with planning permission, outline planning, or a garden plot sold for development (for land, ignore the bedroom and size rules)
a house or bungalow sold explicitly as a development / demolish-and-rebuild plot
exclude: any ordinary house that is not a bungalow (terrace, semi, detached house, cottage) unless sold as a building plot
agricultural or amenity land with no residential planning

gates.text: In one of the search areas above.
Asking at most {price_max}; asking + 1.15W + C at most {allin_max}.
Freehold, or lease of 150+ years with no live covenant dispute.
No movement, subsidence, knotweed, spray foam, non-standard build (Airey, Wimpey no-fines, prefab concrete) or dry rot. Land: no known ground, mining or flood problem.
Vacant possession, and no age restriction or occupancy clause (no over-55 or retirement covenant).

Front door opens into a hall, lobby or porch, never straight into a living, reception or dining room or kitchen. Fail if the listing text or floorplan shows it opens into a room, even if a hall could be made later. If neither shows where it opens, pass as unconfirmed and name it in the risk. Land: pass (the buyer designs the entrance).

Land only: full or outline planning permission for at least one dwelling, or a garden or brownfield plot with written pre-application support; not green belt without consent; vehicle access and services exist or are costed. Bungalows: pass.

finished_spec: 2 good bedrooms (one of 11.5 m2+, ideally a third for an office), one open-plan living-kitchen-dining space of 35 m2+ with good light and no front door into it, front door into a hall, 75-110 m2 inside, all on the ground floor or bedrooms in a dormer. For a building plot: W is the cost to build that house (about £2,400 per m2 plus 12% for fees, services and access), and V is the median of 3 sales of similar new or fully modernised houses or bungalows nearby.

buy_test.tax_note: Stamp duty as a first-time buyer: nil up to £300k, 5% from £300k to £500k.
buy_test.comps_sources: Rightmove sold prices, Zoopla, Land Registry via domovita / housemetric / propertyengine / doogal; Housemetric joins EPC floor areas to sales

criteria.name: £/m² as bought ÷ done-up street £/m² (land: (asking + W) ÷ V per m²)
Floor area now (land: plot fits 90 m²+ house and garden)
Bedrooms
bands: 2 doubles + room for a 3rd or office

criteria.name: Extension headroom (wide or deep plot; loft fits a dormer; neighbours extended)
Street quality (owner-occupied, tidy fronts, few letting boards, no main road or rat-run)
Inside bones (light, ceiling height, scope to open up the single floor, loft height)
Outside (well-built bungalow or good plot, garden, attractive street)
